name: Child and scoped fibers
description: Forking starts an Effect in another fiber. forkChild attaches it to the parent. forkScoped uses the current Scope. forkIn uses a supplied Scope. forkDetach uses the global lifetime. Options include startImmediately and uninterruptible.
good: Background consumers, parallel attempts, and services whose work has an explicit owner.
bad: Persisted work owed after process death. Workflow and SQL-backed delivery belong to that problem. A detached fiber also needs an explicit shutdown policy.

name: Fiber outcomes and interruption

description: Fiber.await returns Exit without propagating failure. Fiber.join propagates the fiber result. Fiber.interrupt requests interruption and waits for termination. Observer and unsafe operations are included on the Fiber interface.
good: Joining work, observing completion, and ending owned background work.
bad: JavaScript CPU preemption or rollback of an accepted external write. Workers address CPU isolation. A provider receipt and idempotency address external writes.

vivid: Uses Fiber.join in apps/server/src/code/pool.ts:142. Candidate manual running array and join loop in apps/server/src/code/process.ts:371 and :391.

name: Interruption masks

bad: Masking an entire unbounded task. Restore interruption for its wait. AbortSignal cannot prove that an external write was undone.

description: FiberSet tracks scoped fibers. FiberMap tracks fibers by key. FiberHandle tracks one fiber. Their run and runtime adapters preserve an owning Scope.

name: Deferred

description: Deferred is a one-shot completion cell for a value or failure. Completion operations return whether they won. complete memoizes the supplied Effect result. completeWith stores the Effect directly.

name: Latch

description: Latch is a reusable gate. open admits current and future waiters. close blocks future waiters. release admits the current waiters while leaving the gate closed.
good: Ready or paused gates with several reopen cycles.
bad: A value-bearing completion or a permit count. Deferred carries a one-shot result. Semaphore counts capacity.

name: Semaphore
exports: make withPermit withPermits withPermitsIfAvailable take takeIfAvailable release resize releaseAll
description: Semaphore counts permits. withPermit and withPermits acquire and release around work. withPermitsIfAvailable returns Option without waiting. take and release expose manual ownership.
good: Process-local locks and capacity bounds. One permit serializes an effectful critical section.
bad: Strict weighted FIFO, bounded admission queues, cross-process locks, or resource pools. Queue, Pool, and a durable database protocol address those shapes. releaseAll does not cancel current holders.

name: PartitionedSemaphore
description: PartitionedSemaphore limits concurrent work independently for each partition key. Its public model exposes the keyed permit wrappers.
good: Per-tenant or per-resource in-process serialization.
bad: Cross-process ownership and custom admission order. SQL claims provide durable authority. A bounded queue can provide an explicit waiting-room policy.

name: Queue and its variants
exports: make bounded dropping sliding unbounded offer offerAll take takeAll takeN takeBetween poll end fail failCause shutdown
description: Queue hands each message to one taker. bounded suspends offers at capacity. dropping rejects excess new items. sliding evicts old items. unbounded grows without a capacity limit. Queue carries an error channel and Done completion.

bad: Broadcast or crash durability. PubSub gives each subscriber a copy. PersistedQueue stores owed work. A sliding queue loses older work by design.

name: PubSub
exports: bounded dropping sliding unbounded subscribe publish publishAll take end shutdown
description: PubSub delivers messages to each current subscription. Bounded storage applies suspend, dropping, or sliding policies. Constructors accept replay for late subscribers. subscribe requires Scope.
good: Process-local fanout with an explicit retention and overflow policy.
bad: Durable cursor replay, database changefeeds, or one-consumer work dispatch. An event log or durable queue supplies different guarantees.
